task.title: feat: runtime client TLS loaders should accept cert-manager key names (tls.crt/tls.key)
task.body:
### Background
When provisioning the runtime mTLS client certificate with cert-manager, the issued Secret uses cert-manager's standard data keys `tls.crt` / `tls.key` (plus `ca.crt`). The runtime client TLS bundle loaders only recognize `client.crt` / `client.key` for the client key pair, so a cert-manager-issued Secret yields server-authenticated TLS only — the client certificate/key pair is silently ignored (directory loader) or rejected as unpaired (Secret loader).

### Issue Type
feature

### Relevant Code
- pkg/utils/runtime/transport.go — `clientCAFile = "ca.crt"`, `clientCertFile = "client.crt"`, `clientKeyFile = "client.key"` are the only recognized names.
  - `NewTLSBundle(dir)` reads `client.crt` / `client.key` from the mounted dir; if both are absent it degrades to server-authenticated TLS.
  - `NewTLSBundleFromSecret(...)` reads the `client.crt` / `client.key` data keys; `ca.crt` is required and honored.
- Consumers: sandbox-manager `--runtime-client-cert-secret` (cmd/sandbox-manager/main.go) and sandbox-controller `--runtime-client-cert-dir` (cmd/agent-sandbox-controller/main.go).

### Notes
- `ca.crt` already matches cert-manager's key, so CA verification works today; only the client key-pair names diverge.
- Directory-mounted consumers can work around this with a Secret volume `items:` remap (tls.crt→client.crt, tls.key→client.key), but the Secret-backed loader used by sandbox-manager reads the Secret through the API and cannot remap.
- The sandbox-gateway runtime mTLS loader already reads tls.crt/tls.key/ca.crt, so the two loaders in this path are inconsistent.

spec: feat: runtime client TLS loaders should accept cert-manager key names (tls.crt/tls.key)
